  • Method Details

    • isEnabled

      public static boolean isEnabled(org.slf4j.Logger log, LogLevel level)
      Tests whether a level is enabled for a logger, using only SLF4J 1.x-compatible Logger methods. This is the equivalent of slf4j 2.x's Logger.isEnabledForLevel, whose parameter type OSHI cannot reference (see LogLevel).

      logAtLevel(Logger, LogLevel, String, Object...) does not need this guard: SLF4J checks the level itself before substituting {} placeholders. Use this only to skip work the caller must perform before the logging call, such as formatting an argument.

      Parameters:
      log - the logger to query
      level - the level to test
      Returns:
      true if the level is enabled for the logger

    • logAtLevel

      public static void logAtLevel(org.slf4j.Logger log, LogLevel level, String msg, Object... args)
      Logs a message at the given level using only SLF4J 1.x-compatible Logger methods (no atLevel fluent API).

      The message is formatted by SLF4J only if the level is enabled, so callers do not need to guard this call with isDebugEnabled() and friends. Use {} placeholders rather than concatenation so that argument substitution remains deferred. Guard with isEnabled(Logger, LogLevel) only when computing an argument is itself expensive.

      SLF4J's implicit-cause handling applies: when the last argument is a Throwable with no matching placeholder, it is attached as the log event's cause rather than substituted into the format string.

      Parameters:
      log - the logger to use
      level - the level at which to log
      msg - the log message, with {} placeholders for the arguments
      args - the arguments to substitute into the message
